Reveria (A05)

Region in the English scoring table: Wescann / Gerudia.

In one sentence: Turn a Gerudian pirate kingdom into a northern maritime power compatible with gnomes, artificery, and overseas trade.

Storytelling: High | Mission-tree length: Long (49 direct missions) | Mission-tree update: local support for EU4 v1.37.5.0; development-branch rework posts require their own version boundary | Distinctiveness: High | Waiting burden: Medium (naval development and reform prerequisites) | Early pressure: Medium | Expansion: High on the coast and overseas, medium inland

A pirate kingdom is not just a nickname

In 1444, Reveria is a feudal kingdom of the Regent Court in Cannor, ruled by Lothane III and carrying a historic feud with Iochand. The offline Wiki records a longer prehistory: in 821, Askel Ironneck laid the foundation during the Gnomish Pass conflict, after which the kingdom grew through raiding, border wars, and maritime connections. Early dynasties repeatedly contested ports with gnomes and neighbouring lords; Reveria was not born as a modern state of technological tolerance. 【Local history script】【Wiki source】

The Manerd Plot of 1131 overthrew the old dynasty and placed the Síl Revers dynasty on the throne, with “Reveria” becoming the formal state name. The kingdom then took Norroy while continuing to compete with Redscale kobolds and gnomes. In 1396, Nimscodd, backed by Gawed, drove its gnomish-pass forces away. That loss leaves 1444 Reveria with maritime ambitions and a real political question about how to treat its gnome neighbours. The Wiki dates belong to its fixed world-lore revision and do not establish the order of current mission completion. 【Wiki source】

From raiders to a mixed kingdom

The local mission tree first asks Reveria to consolidate its ports and coastal strength, then moves toward naval power, trade, overseas colonization, and engineering. It is not merely a pirate bonus tree: its middle phase explicitly promotes accepting Cliff, Creek, and Imperial gnome cultures, building gnomish armies, and writing gnome participation into government reform events. Set against the earlier struggle over the Gnomish Pass, this is a policy turn rather than an institution already completed at game start. 【Local script】【Local flavour text】

Gnomish artificery and organisation change the campaign's feel. Maritime expansion no longer depends only on raiding and fleet size; it also requires bases, technical personnel, a joint army, and later major engineering. Exact values, construction conditions, and route-dependent effects remain governed by the current scripts. Older development logs about artificery provide broad context only; comments calling Reveria a hidden artificer nation do not prove a particular local mission reward. 【Local script】【Related official development log】

The later missions retain Reveria's maritime-power identity through overseas routes, colonization, and major construction. The tension between raider inheritance and multi-group cooperation remains real: whether gnome technology serves only more efficient plunder depends on the route the player follows and the institutions established by the missions. The 49 directly counted missions checked here remain A05 content; no evidence requires changing Tag to continue. 【Local script】

In play, fleets and ports are not a side project to add later. Maritime action affects neighbouring relations and determines whether Reveria can sustain colonial and trade routes. The middle game is about the tempo of gnome policy: recognising cultures, recruiting technical personnel, building a mixed army, and then putting cooperation into government reform form a sequence. Treating gnomes as a one-time military bonus misses the mission tree's theme. Late engineering also requires a durable economic base rather than pirate spoils alone. 【Local script】【Local flavour text】

That makes Reveria different from a country whose only objective is naval conquest. Its long-term drama is whether a kingdom founded on raiding can recognise the capabilities of an old rival and allow those people into its own power structure. The current scripts establish particular gnome cultures and reforms in the route; this article does not have enough evidence to claim that cooperation covers every conquered population. 【Local script】【Wiki source】

Player discussion in 2026 described a “Reveria rework” in a development branch. That is branch-specific context and cannot establish that every preview is present in the user's local v1.37.5.0. This article therefore uses the current mission file for gameplay and does not use search snippets to invent an official Reveria-specific log. 【Community view】

Older player discussions especially praise the contrast between Viking-style raiding and artificer technology; others see the newer missions as flavour and government reform added to a classic structure. Those positions are compatible: the first describes the national fantasy, while the second compares versions. Neither replaces the current scripts. The result is a transformation that carries the pirate past outward rather than abandoning it. 【Community view】

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 75/100 | Autocracy 61/100 | Magic↔Artifice 18/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 76/100) | Pluralism 75/100. The phase shift is early pirate kingdom (Pluralism 42) → gnome co-rule reform (Pluralism 75).

The v2.1 value profile is Neutral (66/100), with an improving trajectory. Gnome cultural acceptance, military participation, and government involvement provide positive institutional evidence; the raiding tradition lowers restraint, but colonization or naval expansion alone cannot establish evil. Gnome inclusion and institutional participation are positive evidence, while raiding and maritime policy may harm others; the word “colonization” alone does not establish evil. Existing checks do not prove that co-rule extends to every group, so confidence remains moderate. This suits players who want a pirate-kingdom transformation, naval and artificery development, and a historic enemy becoming a technical partner; it does not suit players who want only conventional inland conquest or who do not want port and overseas objectives. 【Local script】【Wiki source】

See the evidence page for source files, fixed Wiki revisions, and version boundaries. The English translation receipt is bilingual-v235-text-A05-review.md.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and scripted effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as idea groups are filled, and the ambition applies after all seven have been unlocked. Racial, government and mission rewards are excluded. Successor ideas do not automatically stack with predecessor ideas. Descriptions may recall history or portray future ideals, not automatically events already completed in 1444. Native English originals are reused rather than back-translating expanded Chinese localisation. Inherited effect values and unresolved units remain qualified without changing Chinese source data.

Reveria (A05) — Reverian Ideas

Traditions: Reverian Traditions

Effects: Army morale: +10%; National unrest: -1.

Idea 1: The Portroy Agreement

During the Era of Black Ice, our ancestors sailed from Old Gerudia south to the bountiful land of Lencenor. Through strength we forced the Lorentish King to recognize all lands north of the Portroy river as rightfully ours, establishing a proud heritage of independence for our people. As proven many times in the past, we will fight to defend ourselves and what is ours from any enemy, be they Gawedi, Lorentish, or otherwise!

Effects: War exhaustion: -0.03.

Idea 2: Between Two Giants

Reveria's independence has always been contingent on the willingness of Gawed and Lorent to cooperate with us against the other. Luckily, we have wisely used our position to forge alliances with houses on both sides, so as to discourage either from attacking us directly.

Effects: Diplomatic relations: +1; Improve relations: +10%.

Idea 3: Poleaxe Mastery

In days past, the footmen of Reveria were highly skilled axe-men, unrivalled in their ability across the world. However, with the innovations in cavalry techniques in Lorent to our south and in the Empire itself, our axe-men have become somewhat obsolete. This has led us to adopt a new weapon, the poleaxe. Far more effective at dealing with cavalry, this weapon has made it so that our opponents' knights think twice before charging our battle lines.

Effects: shock_damage_received：-10%.

Idea 4: Second Age of Reavers

With the rediscovery of Aelantir, and the wealth it has brought, an opportunity has arisen for us. As in days past, we shall punish the decadent and arrogant coastal powers. We shall raid their settlements, sink their fleets, and bleed them dry. Our time has come, The Second Age of Reavers has officially begun!

Effects: Privateer efficiency: +15%.

Idea 5: Reaping the Harvests

While not the first to have inhabited this land, we are its current custodians. It might not be the most bountiful, but it has sustained our people for generations. In order to better utilize the land, our government has over the past few decades announced multiple reforms to our administration, specifically regarding crop quotas and land ownerships. These laws have both massively improved the efficiency of our farms, and has also allowed local disputes to be more easily settled.

Effects: Development cost: -10%.

Idea 6: Gnomish Intelligentsia

The first locals the Reavers encountered when landing on these coasts were in fact gnomes, who promptly redirected the northern raiders to the most plump and lucrative human villages… for a cut of the spoils, of course. Ever since then, the gnomish peoples have found a safe home in Reveria, forming the backbone of the country's scholarly and innovative circles.

Effects: Technology cost: -5%.

Idea 7: Axe-Pistols of Reveria

While an odd invention, the axe-pistol has become an infamous symbol of our armed forces across Cannor. Standard Equipment for all officers, the axe-pistol allows the best of the Reverian Army to showcase that the blood of old Gerudia and its ancestral huscarl elites still flows, alive and well, in Reveria.

Effects: Infantry combat ability: +10%.

Ambition: Reverian Ambition

Effects: Movement speed: +10%.
